title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while the vehicles sat in heavy traffic. The deployed system failed to manage its energy consumption under congestion conditions it encountered, leaving at least a dozen vehicles immobilized and requiring roadside assistance to clear them. This failure happened in real-world traffic, not in testing, where the vehicles were actively carrying passengers or waiting for rides during an unplanned traffic event.

The vehicles were deployed in a city at a time of year and a location where major public events predictably cause gridlock. Catching this failure before deployment would have required stress-testing the battery management system under realistic sustained congestion scenarios, including heavy traffic lasting hours, and designing either sufficient energy reserves or a graceful degradation protocol to move vehicles to safety rather than strand them. It is not established whether the system was designed with traffic surge capacity for predictable public events or whether operators were aware the vehicles lacked adequate resilience for the conditions they encountered.

Waymo had faced a related challenge months earlier when a power outage affected traffic signal operation in the same city, suggesting a pattern of insufficient planning for infrastructure disruptions that affect traffic flow.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high volume of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen resilience during major traffic disruptions.

The incident caused frustration among other drivers caught in the standstill, with some spending nearly two hours in traffic. One passenger reported a Waymo vehicle drove when fireworks were being set off on the street, and another vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to have conversations with public and private partners about the traffic situation. This marks another challenge for Waymo in San Francisco, following a December incident when service paused during a major power outage that affected traffic lights.
